events.title: Labour Day
events.description: Labour Day in Canada is celebrated on the first Monday of September. It originally gave workers the chance to campaign for better working conditions or pay. The day is now part of a long weekend for many Canadians.

events.title: International Literacy Day
events.description:
A day to raise people’s awareness of and concern for literacy issues in the world. (International)

 International Literacy Day (ILD) will be celebrated under the theme of “Promoting literacy in the digital era.”

events.title: World suicide prevention day
events.description:
World Suicide Prevention Day is observed on September 10 each year to raise awareness of suicide and to promote action through proven means that will reduce the number of suicides and suicide attempts globally. (International)
This year's theme is all about 'Creating Hope Through Action. '

events.title: International Week of Deaf People
events.description:
The International Week of Deaf People was first celebrated in September 1958 and has since evolved into a global movement of deaf unity and concerted advocacy to raise awareness of the issues deaf people face in their everyday lives. (International).
Theme for 2025: No Human Rights Without Sign Language Rights

events.title: International Day of Peace
events.description: The International Day of Peace 2025 theme is “Cultivating a Culture of Peace.” This year marks the 25th anniversary of the United Nations General Assembly's adoption of the Declaration and Programme of Action on a Culture of Peace.

events.title: International Day of Sign Languages
events.description:
The International Day of Sign Languages is a unique opportunity to support and protect the linguistic iidentity and cultural diversity of all deaf people and other sign language users. Celebrated annually across the world on 23 September every year along with the International Week of Deaf People. (International)

Theme: Sign Language Rights for All!

events.title: Gender Equality Week
events.description:
Gender Equality Week, the fourth week in September, is an opportunity to raise awareness of the important
contributions women and gender diverse communities have made to the growth, development, character
and identity of Canada.

events.title:
National Day for Truth and
Reconciliation / Orange Shirt Day
events.description:
The day honours the lost children and Survivors of residential schools, their families and communities.
Public commemoration of the tragic and painful history and ongoing impacts of residential schools is  vital component of the reconciliation process. The creation of this federal statutory holiday was through  legislative amendments made by Parliament.
